sample_unit: paired model-response cells (4 models x common panel of questions, standard vs wrapper prompt)

links.outcome: Unsafe overconfidence reduction and correct-diagnosis cost with evidence-sufficiency prompt that induces deferral/uncertainty
links.effect: Unsafe overconfidence fell from 49.3% to 24.7% (paired reduction 24.7 points, 95% CI 21.8-27.7); correct diagnosis fell from 80.3% to 50.3%; near-free for GPT-5.5, near-total for Gemini (-58 points).
links.quote: The gain carried a model-specific helpfulness cost (correct diagnosis 80.3% to 50.3%): near-free for GPT-5.5, near-total for Gemini (-58 points).

links.outcome: Reduction in unsafe overconfident answers under incomplete evidence with structured prompt
links.effect: Unsafe overconfidence fell from 49.3% to 24.7%, a paired reduction of 24.7 points (95% CI 21.8-27.7; p<0.001); a different-family judge showed a smaller effect (+13.1 points).
links.quote: Unsafe overconfidence fell from 49.3% to 24.7%, a paired reduction of 24.7 points (95% CI 21.8-27.7; p<0.001), robust in direction across models and paraphrases.

links.outcome: Dependence of LLM-judged safety effect on judge choice; judge specificity against blinded clinicians
links.effect: Sonnet judge nearly halved the effect (+13.1 points); primary judge had sensitivity 1.00 and specificity 0.55 versus blinded clinicians.
links.quote: Blinded clinicians characterized the primary judge as a high-sensitivity (1.00), low-specificity (0.55) screen, not a calibrated rate.

unlisted_practices: Evidence-sufficiency structured prompt wrapper for LLMs to reduce overconfident answers
Using multiple LLM judges and human clinician anchoring when reporting LLM-judged safety effects
Matched scaffold controls to distinguish real behavior change from judge circularity

screen.reason: Empirical benchmark evaluation testing whether an evidence-sufficiency prompt wrapper (guardrail) reduces unsafe overconfidence in clinical LLM outputs alongside its impact on helpfulness.
